questionText: $f(x)$ and $g(y)$ are functions of $x$ and $y$, respectively, and $f(x) = g(y)$ for all real values of $x$ and $y$. Which one of the following options is necessarily TRUE for all $x$ and $y$?
explanation:
Given that $f(x) = g(y)$ for all real values of $x$ and $y$.

Since $f(x)$ depends solely on $x$ and $g(y)$ depends solely on $y$, varying $x$ cannot change the value of $g(y)$, and varying $y$ cannot change the value of $f(x)$.

For the equality $f(x) = g(y)$ to hold true across all possible independent real values of $x$ and $y$, both functions must evaluate to the same constant value for every input.

Therefore, $f(x) = g(y) = \text{constant}$ is necessarily true.

Hence, option (B) is the correct choice.
